direction.comments: The direction on a macroscale is very much your typical '70s and '80s crime thriller, with the look and feel of that era as it builds its world in 1986 Queens, even ending with a split diopter shot that's very '80s; the direction on a microscale makes it feel more like a play, with a lot of speaking and performances since there really isn't much plot to go through, but the performances are good and the cast has good chemistry, which makes those scenes enjoyable and memorable; the storytelling is fine but not the best, as the movie is so slow and has so little plot to get through that it feels like a drag; the tension is built decently well, as you really see the impact this crime and working with the mob have on the family and how stressed the characters are, and the climax is very tense and executed very well

performance.comments: Gives a good performance, and even though I haven't seen him act well in a while, he comes back for this one, carrying his scenes and the movie as the lead while having good chemistry with Miles Teller and Scarlett Johansson

A little over the top, but she plays this '80s caricature of a housewife well and gives a good performance that shows why she's a two-time Oscar-nominated actress, and she has good chemistry with Miles Teller and Adam Driver
One of the best performances I've seen from him lately, as he does the accent work very well, has good chemistry with Scarlett Johansson, and very much makes his scenes memorable

cast.comments: There isn't much of a cast beyond the leads, but everyone is fine and does a good job supporting the main cast

story.comments: The concept is your typical '80s crime drama, very much emulating the crime dramas of that era; the plot structure is very linear with not much plot to go through, and you could trim this nearly two-hour movie to 90 minutes, but I don't think you'd want to, because it's paced like The Godfather, and a slow pace like that only works with a continuous payoff, which The Godfather had across almost three hours of content, while the payoff here is so small, as the climax is executed well but isn't the best or most satisfying ending from a plot perspective; character writing gets the job done, as you understand who these characters are and the relationship between the brothers is fine, even if it's not the best writing and Scarlett Johansson's character is a little over the top, but I didn't care about any of them

screenplay.comments: The dialogue is very emblematic of dialogue-heavy '70s and '80s crime dramas, but it feels a little clunky and not that well written, though it gets the job done and isn't the worst dialogue ever; the humor shows up in some moments, but humor isn't really what this movie is about; the symbolism is a big part of the movie, as it's a lot about corruption and dealing with the mob, which is what crime dramas from that era represent, and it does a good job showing that; the foreshadowing is fine, as it's not the best work but does its job

score.comments: Mainly used in transitions from one scene to another, and while it's well composed and does a pretty good job in those moments, it's used so sparingly that a lot of the interpersonal scenes feel dull and bland without a score to amplify them and set the tone, so I would have liked to see them use it more as a storytelling tool

cinematography.comments: The constant lens flares really annoyed me because there are so many of them, though it's kind of meta since the flares blind the characters too, and otherwise it's fine, shot on film in a very wide aspect ratio that looks like other James Gray movies and feels like an '80s movie

editing.comments: Fine, as it works in conjunction with the flares and uses a lot of fades

sound.comments: Pretty good and well put together, as it makes the crime drama parts memorable and really makes the climax tense, and while it's nothing substantial since there aren't many action sequences for a crime drama, it does a pretty good job in the ones that are there

production_design.comments: Very much transports you to 1980s New York, and I very much enjoyed the look and feel it gives the movie

makeup.comments: Actually good, making Miles Teller's and Scarlett Johansson's characters look good and like they're from the '80s

costumes.comments: Pretty good, as they transport you to the 1980s, especially with how they make Miles Teller's and Scarlett Johansson's characters look like they're from that era

review.pacing: The biggest issue, as it has the pacing of The Godfather with half the plot and a much shorter runtime, so there's only so much it can cover, and this is one of the few times I'd actually add time to a movie, as another 30 minutes would make the payoff at the end worth more, so if there's ever a director's cut, I'd really like to see it
review.climax: Executed well, with action that's pretty tense and shot very well, and while it's not the best climax ever and only somewhat satisfying as an ending, the movie as a whole leaves me unsatisfied because the payoff isn't that great
review.tone: Very much your '70s and '80s crime drama in the vein of The Godfather
review.final_notes: Got sent a screener for this
review.overall: Overall, 'Paper Tiger' is carried by its performances and aesthetic, with memorable interpersonal scenes that transport you to a classic '80s crime thriller, and while it's very emblematic of The Godfather, it pairs that movie's slow pacing with a much shorter runtime, leaving very little plot to go through and a payoff at the end that doesn't feel that satisfying
